Tosafot on Bava Batra 57b:1:1.hebrew: בשותפין עסקינן דבהעמדה כדי לא קפדי - תימה: דאמר הכא דהיכא דקפדי קני, והאמר לעיל (בבא בתרא דף מב:) דשותפין אין מחזיקין זה על זה, דפעמים מניח האחד להשתמש לחברו ג' שנים ואח"כ ישתמש הוא? י"ל: הא דנחית לפלגא, והא דנחית לכולא, להאי גיסא או להאי גיסא, כדאמר לעיל. ועוד נראה דיש לחלק בין שדה לחצר: דהכא מיירי שבתים אלו פתוחין לחצר זה, דכיון שהוא יוצא ונכנס דרך חצר זה, היכא דקפדי אין מניח לו לעשות, אי לאו דזבנה מיניה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 57b:1:1.english: "We are dealing with partners, for regarding placing [an object] temporarily they are not particular" - This is puzzling: For [the Gemara] says here that where they are particular, [the one who remained silent] acquires [the right]. But did it not say earlier (Bava Batra 42b) that partners cannot establish a presumptive claim [of ownership] against one another, because sometimes one [partner] lets his fellow make use [of the property] for three years, and afterward he himself will make use of it? One can answer: This case [in the earlier passage] is where he entered [and took possession of] half, whereas this case is where he entered [and took possession of] the whole, on this side or that side, as stated earlier. Furthermore, it appears that one can distinguish between a field and a courtyard: For here [the Gemara] is speaking of a case where these houses open into this courtyard, so that since he [the other partner] goes in and out by way of this courtyard, where they are particular he would not allow him to do [it], had he not purchased it from him.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 57b:2:1.hebrew: אסור ליכנס בחצר - בגמ' מוקי לה בין בחצר שיש בה דין חלוקה בין אין בה. ואע"ג דבאין בה דין חלוקה אין יכול למחות בו מליכנס בחצר, מ"מ יכול לאסור עליו, מידי דהוה אמשכיר בית לחברו שיכול המשכיר להקדישו, כדאמר בפ' האומר משקלי עלי (ערכין דף כא. ושם), אע"פ שאין יכול למחות בידו של שוכר מליכנס בו. ומיהו היא גופא תימה: מ"ש מבעל חוב, דאם הקדיש שדהו דאתי בעל חוב ושקיל (שם כג:)? אלא משום דרבי אבהו, שלא יאמרו הקדש יוצא לחולין בלא פדיון — מוסיף דינר. וי"ל דשאני בע"ח, שגוף הקרקע יוצא מתחת יד מקדיש, אבל התם אין גוף הקרקע יוצא מתחת יד משכיר לעולם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 57b:2:1.english: It is forbidden to enter the courtyard - In the Gemara, it is established [that this applies] both to a courtyard that is subject to the law of division and to one that is not. And although [in a courtyard] that is not subject to the law of division he cannot protest against [the other's] entering the courtyard, nevertheless he can prohibit [the property] to him [through a vow], just as in the case of one who rents a house to his fellow, where the lessor can consecrate it, as stated in the chapter "HaOmer Mishkali Alai" (Arakhin 21a and there), even though he cannot protest against the renter's entering it. But this itself is puzzling: how is this different from a creditor, [for whom we rule] that if [the debtor] consecrated his field, the creditor comes and takes it (ibid. 23b)? Rather, [it is] because of Rabbi Abahu — so that people not say that consecrated property goes out to non-sacred status without redemption — [the creditor] adds a dinar. And one can answer that a creditor is different, since the substance of the land leaves the possession of the one who consecrated it, whereas there, the substance of the land never leaves the possession of the lessor.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 57b:5:1.hebrew: רבינא אמר לעולם לא קפדי - משמע הכא דכולי עלמא קפדי אינשי אדריסת הרגל, דאפי' רבינא לא קאמר אלא בשותפין. ותימה, דתנן בפ"ק דמגילה (דף ח. ושם ד"ה דריסת): "אין בין המודר הנאה מחבירו למודר הימנו מאכל אלא דריסת הרגל וכלים שאין עושין בהן אוכל נפש", ופריך בגמ': דריסת הרגל הא לא קפדי? ומפרש ר"ת דהתם משמע ליה לגמרא דמתני' איירי בבקעה דלא קפדי, דאי בחצר דקפדי, אפילו מודר הימנו מאכל אסור; דכיון דקפדי, א"כ כיוצא בו משכירים, ותנן בפרק אין בין המודר (נדרים דף לג.) דכיוצא בו משכירים אסור, אפילו כלים שאין עושין בהן אוכל נפש. ולהכי פריך: כיון דעל כרחך איירי בדריסת הרגל בבקעה דלא קפדי, אם כן אפילו מודר הימנו הנאה אמאי אסור? והוא הדין דהוי מצי למיפרך "כלים הא לא קפדי":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 57b:5:1.english: Ravina said: Actually, they are not particular - It implies here that everyone is particular about people treading on their property, since even Ravina says [that they are not particular] only with regard to partners. And this is puzzling, for we learned in the first chapter of Megillah (8a; see there, s.v. deriset): "The only differences between one who is prohibited by vow from deriving benefit from his fellow and one who is prohibited from [eating] his food are walking on [the fellow's property] and utensils with which food is not prepared," and the Gemara asks there: [Regarding] walking on his property, are people not particular about that? And Rabbeinu Tam explains that there the Gemara understood that the Mishnah is dealing with a field [bik'ah], where people are not particular; for if it were [dealing with] a courtyard, where they are particular, even one who is prohibited from [eating] his food would be forbidden. For since they are particular, then [it is a case where] they would rent out something similar to it, and we learned in the chapter "Ein Bein HaMudar" (Nedarim 33a) that where they rent out something similar to it, it is forbidden, even [for] utensils with which food is not prepared. And therefore [the Gemara] asks: Since you must say that [the Mishnah] is dealing with walking in a field, where they are not particular, then why is even one who is prohibited from deriving benefit from him forbidden [to walk there]? And by the same reasoning, it could have asked about utensils: Are people not particular about those?
